mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this hypothesis remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and thus predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this hypothesis remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods where RSAFS shows sustained growth, or if the Rank IC for this hypothesis remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a contraction in supply, leading to reduced economic output and negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this hypothesis remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a single month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and thus predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this hypothesis remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in the same period, signals a robust demand environment and a strengthening labor market, which together predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases over 3 months and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this hypothesis remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a loosening monetary policy, which is expected to stimulate economic activity and positively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this hypothesis remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which is expected to boost corporate earnings and positively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods where GDPC1 shows sustained growth, or if the Rank IC for this hypothesis remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
